note: v1, written: NIGHT FREIGHT. Instrumental post-metal (the style board's t3 row): a freight train crosses the album at night, and the wheels' clack over the rail joints becomes the riff's odd meter. 132 bpm, B minor in drop-tuned guitars. 7/8 (the wheels) against 4/4 (the crescendo). Seven movements, 8:10. I CROSSING: a level-crossing bell; the freight's rumble swells; synthesised wheel clacks rise on a 14-sixteenth cycle; the horn's three tones drop a semitone as it passes. II JOINTS: a clean 8-string arpeggio riff of seven eighths (2+2+3) on the clack rhythm, fretless bass, rims, then toms. III CHUG: the riff drop-tuned on doubled m8 rigs (palm-muted 16ths into an open power chord), fuzz bass, sub, a room kit with ride; a tremolo-picked lead plays THE LINE. IV YARD: the train gone; wind, distant metal in a 6 s yard hall every 5 bars, a cello drone, the ebow sings THE LINE augmented. V CLIMB: 4/4 - the clean riff stretched to eight eighths over growing toms, the bass walking the riff inverted, then tremolo walls (power chords picked in 16ths) and the ebow an octave up, the kit to full. VI DERAILED: half-time doom in A (A C Bb | A G | C Bb | G A), china, sub, and the wheels' 7 back against the 4. VII LAST CAR: the clean riff alone with the bell, the horn far away and lower, the clacks fading, wind. note: v2, written: FREIGHT BY SEA, and the movements develop. (1) Off the rails: The Last Train (t6) is built on a synthesised train too, so trains are chirper-three's. Night Freight moves to a container port at night. A gantry crane's chain clanking through its sheave keeps the 14-sixteenth cycle and the riff's 7/8; a buoy bell is struck by the swell at irregular gaps; waves; a ship's diesel throbs (brown noise and a 46 Hz hum under a 2.7 Hz tremolo); the foghorn sounds two low tones (B, F#); the yard becomes the container stacks: containers set down, air brakes, a reversing alarm far off. (2) THE OPERATOR, the album's synthesised speech done small and close: a crane operator on a handheld intercom (voice-speech, ARPAbet, walkie-talkie band and drive), "seven, clear to lift" (the seven is the meter), "lowering", "hold"; at the end "last one, lights stay on". (3) No looping: the 64-bar chug runs in four stages: the riff; its grouping rotated 3+2+2; THE LINE over it; stabs on every group over double kick, and a one-stab break into the stacks. A second guitar's natural harmonics answer the clean riff in the joints. The undertow's doom thins in its last 8 bars to one held A chord every two bars, with an ebow crying A-G-E.
